problem.text: A point $P$ is chosen in the interior of $\triangle ABC$ such that when lines are drawn through $P$ parallel to the sides of $\triangle ABC$, the resulting smaller triangles $t_1$, $t_2$, and $t_3$ in the figure, have areas $4$, $9$, and $49$, respectively. Find the area of $\triangle ABC$.

steps.title: Where to start: parallel lines make similar triangles
steps.body: Each small triangle has its three sides parallel to the three sides of $\triangle ABC$, so it has the same angles and is similar to $\triangle ABC$. For similar triangles, the ratio of areas is the square of the ratio of sides. The areas $4$, $9$, $49$ are perfect squares, which is a strong hint to take square roots.

your_turn.prompt: What is the ratio of the sides of $t_1$, $t_2$ and $t_3$?

steps.title: Name the sides parallel to $BC$
steps.body: Let the sides of $t_1$, $t_2$, $t_3$ that are parallel to $BC$ be $2x$, $3x$ and $7x$. The side of $t_3$ lies right on $BC$. The rest of $BC$ is the bottom of the two parallelograms at the lower left and lower right corners.

your_turn.prompt: The lower-left parallelogram has its top side on the horizontal line through $P$. That top side is a side of which small triangle, and how long is the bottom side of the parallelogram?
your_turn.answer: It is the side of $t_1$, so it is $2x$. Opposite sides of a parallelogram are equal, so the bottom piece of $BC$ is also $2x$.

steps.title: Add up the pieces of $BC$
steps.body: In the same way, the top of the lower-right parallelogram is the side of $t_2$, so its bottom piece of $BC$ is $3x$. So $BC$ splits into three pieces coming from $t_1$, $t_3$ and $t_2$. Careful: each piece matches a different triangle, so all three of $2x$, $3x$, $7x$ appear once.

your_turn.prompt: Write the length of $BC$ in terms of $x$.

steps.title: Put it together
steps.body:
Compare $\triangle ABC$ with $t_1$: the sides are in ratio $12x : 2x = 6$, so the area of $\triangle ABC$ is $6^2$ times the area of $t_1$:
$$[ABC] = 6^2 \cdot 4 = 144.$$
The answer is **$144$**.
